Aegis Clinical Networks Scheduling Eligibility Guidelines v4.2

1. Purpose & Scope
These guidelines establish the mandatory criteria for provider onboarding, patient appointment routing, and procedure authorization within the Aegis Clinical Networks ecosystem. All scheduling coordinators, clinical managers, revenue cycle auditors, and regional directors must adhere to these standards to maintain network compliance. The document governs booking protocols, credentialing validation, and capacity management across all twelve operating facilities. Section 1.4 Precedence Hierarchy: In the event of a direct conflict between base operational criteria (Section 2) and active pilot program directives (Section 6), pilot program directives shall prevail without further administrative review. Base criteria remain the default standard for all non-pilot operations and general network routing.

2. Base Provider & Procedure Criteria
Providers must hold an unexpired state medical license and a valid DEA registration to be entered into the scheduling matrix. All elective procedures require written pre-authorization submitted to the central registry at least five business days prior to the scheduled date. Credentialing files must be updated every twenty-four months; failure to renew by the expiration date results in an automatic fourteen-day scheduling freeze. Providers specializing in interventional radiology must additionally complete the Aegis Advanced Imaging Certification module before their first scheduled case. Billing codes must align with the current CPT edition; mismatched codes trigger a financial hold until corrected by the revenue cycle team. The following table outlines base credentialing thresholds:
| Credential Category | Renewal Cycle | Required Documentation | Scheduling Impact if Lapsed |
|---------------------|---------------|------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Medical License     | 24 months     | State board verification | 14-day freeze              |
| DEA Registration    | 36 months     | Federal agency stamp   | Immediate booking halt      |
| Board Certification | 10 years      | Specialty board letter | Restricted to consult only  |

3. Standard Scheduling Windows & Patient Triage
Standard outpatient consultations require a minimum seventy-two-hour advance notice from the booking timestamp to the appointment start time. This seventy-two-hour window ensures adequate clinical preparation and room turnover. Triage Level 1 cases (acute pain, suspected fracture) may be compressed to a twenty-four-hour window upon physician override. Triage Level 2 cases (chronic management, post-op check) must adhere strictly to the seventy-two-hour standard. Triage Level 3 cases (routine wellness, medication refill) are restricted to calendar slots opening on the first business day of the following month. No patient may be double-booked across overlapping time blocks without explicit dual-physician sign-off. Scheduling coordinators must verify insurance eligibility before locking any slot exceeding the seventy-two-hour threshold.

4. Compensation Tiers & Notice Modifications
Provider compensation tiers directly influence scheduling flexibility. Tier-1 Standard providers operate under the baseline notice requirements outlined in Section 3. Tier-2 Rapid Access providers, defined as those maintaining a patient satisfaction score above 4.8/5.0 and a cancellation rate below 2%, qualify for modified scheduling parameters. Tier-2 providers may accept bookings with a twenty-four-hour advance notice, overriding the standard seventy-two-hour requirement. Tier-3 Elite providers receive priority placement in high-demand slots but must maintain a minimum twenty-eight-day advance notice for all non-urgent procedures to preserve calendar integrity. Tier assignments are recalculated quarterly based on the preceding ninety-day performance window. Financial penalties for missed slots are calculated at $150 per hour for Tier-1, $200 per hour for Tier-2, and $250 per hour for Tier-3.

5. Clinical Volume & Capacity Limits
To prevent clinical burnout and ensure care quality, daily procedure caps are enforced. Primary care providers are limited to sixteen patient encounters per operational day. Surgical specialists are capped at four major procedures or eight minor procedures daily. When a provider reaches ninety percent of their daily cap, the scheduling system automatically locks new bookings for that day and routes requests to the overflow queue. Overflow cases are assigned to on-call backup providers who must respond within four hours. Exceptions to volume caps require written approval from the Chief Medical Officer and are logged as variance events for monthly review. Monthly volume reports are generated on the 15th and must be reconciled by the 20th.

6. Special Programs & Pilot Waivers
The Aegis Regional Access Initiative (RAI) is a twelve-month pilot program launched on October 1, 2023, designed to expand care in underserved zip codes. Participating providers in RAI zones are granted specific scheduling exemptions to increase throughput. RAI participants may bypass the standard twenty-four-month credentialing renewal freeze if they submit a provisional renewal packet within seven days of expiration. Additionally, RAI providers are permitted to schedule elective procedures with only three business days of written pre-authorization, provided the patient resides within an RAI-designated county. Participation is voluntary and requires a signed Memorandum of Understanding with the regional director. Pilot funding is capped at $450,000 annually per participating facility.

7. Compliance & Audit Triggers
Routine audits are conducted on scheduling logs exceeding fifty entries per month. Providers triggering an audit must submit time-stamped clinical notes for a random sample of twenty percent of scheduled cases. The general pre-authorization timeline applies universally; however, pediatric oncology follow-ups and emergency trauma cases are explicitly exempt from the five-day written pre-authorization requirement. These exempt categories may proceed with a twenty-four-hour verbal attestation documented in the electronic health record within two hours of the encounter. Failure to document the verbal attestation within the two-hour window converts the case to a standard billing hold. Audit findings are reported to the compliance committee on the third Friday of each month.

8. Effective Dates & Amendments
These guidelines took effect on January 15, 2024, replacing the previous Q4 2023 scheduling protocols. Amendments are issued annually or upon regulatory change. The version control tag appears in the document header; coordinators must verify they are referencing version 4.2 or later. Oakhaven Manufacturing Ltd. Employee Benefits Summary (Effective January 1, 2024)

1. Eligibility & Employment Classification
All benefit provisions outlined in this summary apply exclusively to full-time permanent staff members of Oakhaven Manufacturing Ltd. who have completed a continuous service period of 184 days. Contract workers, temporary agency placements, and interns are expressly excluded from all programs described herein. Employment classification is determined by the number of contracted weekly hours; roles requiring 32 hours or more per week are designated as Tier 1, while roles requiring 20 to 31 hours are designated as Tier 2. Tier 2 employees are ineligible for any benefits marked with an asterisk (*) in subsequent sections. Probationary periods of up to 90 days do not count toward the 184-day continuous service requirement unless the employee receives a written extension of their probation date prior to the 90-day mark.

2. Health & Dental Insurance Parameters
Medical and dental coverage commences on the first day of the month following the completion of the 184-day service threshold. The standard plan covers 80% of eligible medical expenses after a $1,500 individual deductible is met. Dental coverage operates on a separate $300 annual deductible and reimburses 70% of preventive care and 50% of major procedures. Dependents are eligible for inclusion provided they are under the age of 26, or over 26 if they meet the IRS definition of a qualifying child or disabled adult child. Spouses may be added regardless of age, provided a valid marriage certificate is submitted within 60 days of the wedding date. Coverage for domestic partners requires submission of a notarized cohabitation agreement or a joint lease agreement dated within the last 12 months. Alternative documentation may be accepted if it demonstrates primary residence sharing, subject to regional compliance review. Legal documentation of shared financial responsibility, such as joint bank accounts or shared utility bills, does not satisfy the domestic partner requirement.

3. Retirement & Savings Contribution Limits
The Oakhaven 401(k) plan allows employee contributions up to 25% of gross annual salary, subject to IRS annual limits. The company matches 50% of employee contributions up to the first 6% of salary. For employees in the Financial Services division, a supplemental deferred compensation plan is available, allowing additional pre-tax deferrals up to $50,000 annually. Vesting for company matches follows a graded schedule: 20% per year of service, fully vested at year 5. Early withdrawal penalties apply to distributions taken before age 59½, except for qualified hardship withdrawals or loans up to $50,000 or 50% of vested balance, whichever is less. For employees who relocate using company funds, all ancillary housing and location-based stipends are suspended for 12 months following the move date. Loan repayment must be completed within 60 months.

4. Leave Entitlements & Accrual Schedules
Paid Time Off (PTO) accrues at a rate of 1.2 days per month for Tier 1 employees and 0.8 days per month for Tier 2 employees. Unused PTO may be carried forward up to a maximum of 15 days into the following calendar year; any balance exceeding 15 days is forfeited on December 31. Sick leave is tracked separately and accrues at 0.5 days per month, with a cap of 20 days. The *Unlimited Wellness Days* program applies exclusively to employees holding a Band 5 or higher leadership designation. Band 5+ employees may take up to 5 wellness days per quarter without deducting from their PTO or sick leave balances, provided they submit a manager approval form 48 hours in advance. All other leave requests, including bereavement (3 days) and jury duty (unlimited, paid at base rate), must be logged in the HR portal within 5 business days of occurrence.

5. Educational Assistance & Certification Funding
Oakhaven supports continuous learning through the Professional Development Fund (PDF). Eligibility requires a minimum of 365 days of continuous service and a current performance rating of "Meets Expectations" or higher. Funding is allocated according to the following rubric:
- Tier A (Full Funding): Covers 100% of tuition, fees, and required textbooks for degrees directly related to the employee's current department. Requires a signed service agreement committing to remain with the company for 24 months post-completion.
- Tier B (Partial Funding): Covers 60% of tuition and fees for degree programs outside the employee's direct department or for standalone elective courses. Requires a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 throughout the program.
- Tier C (Stipend Only): Provides a flat $1,000 annual stipend for non-degree certifications, workshops, or conference attendance. No GPA requirement.
Applications must be submitted before the semester start date. Reimbursement is processed within 30 days of submitting a verified transcript showing course completion. If a course is dropped after the add/drop deadline, no reimbursement is issued for that specific course.

6. Relocation, Remote Work & Hardship Allowances
Employees transferring to a new metropolitan area more than 50 miles from their current worksite are eligible for the Standard Relocation Package, which covers moving company fees, temporary housing for up to 30 days, and a one-time settlement allowance of $2,500. The Remote Work Stipend of $750 annually is available to employees who maintain a primary residence outside the designated corporate hub radius. This stipend is disbursed in two equal installments on July 1 and January 1. Employees who receive the Standard Relocation Package are explicitly barred from claiming the Remote Work Stipend for the same calendar year. Hardship allowances for cost-of-living adjustments are calculated quarterly based on regional CPI indices and are applied directly to base salary, not as a separate taxable benefit.

7. Policy Hierarchy & Interpretation Guidelines
In the event of any ambiguity, contradiction, or overlapping eligibility criteria between different sections of this benefits summary, the following hierarchy shall apply. First, specific rider documents or addendums issued after the effective date of January 1, 2024, override general policy statements. Second, if two general policy statements conflict, the provision with the narrower scope or more restrictive conditions prevails. Third, departmental handbooks do not supersede this master summary; they serve only as implementation guides. All monetary values are fixed in USD and are not subject to automatic inflation adjustments unless explicitly stated. The Human Resources Compliance Office holds final interpretive authority on all benefit disputes.

8. Claims Submission & Audit Procedures
All benefit claims, including healthcare reimbursements, educational funding requests, and stipend disbursements, must be submitted via the internal MyBenefits portal. Supporting documentation must be uploaded in PDF format and must not exceed 10 MB per file. Claims submitted outside the 90-day window following the service date or expense occurrence will be automatically rejected. For educational assistance, the transcript must be uploaded directly from the institution's secure portal; student-generated PDFs are not accepted. If a claim requires manual review due to missing documentation, alternative evidence submission, or system errors, the processing timeline extends to 60 days. Employees may appeal a rejection within 15 business days by submitting a formal review request to the Compliance Office, citing the specific policy clause believed to have been misapplied.

AssetCare Maintenance Request Form & Reviewer Guidelines

1. Submission Guidelines & Departmental Quotas
All maintenance requests must be submitted via the centralised AssetCare portal no later than 17:00 local time on the business day preceding the requested service date. Forms submitted after this deadline are automatically queued for the next available operational cycle. Each submission requires a unique tracking identifier formatted as MC-[Year]-[DeptCode]-[Seq]. Digital signatures from both the requesting technician and the designated departmental lead are mandatory before the form enters the review pipeline. Incomplete forms lacking asset serial numbers, failure descriptions, or preliminary cost estimates will be rejected within two business days without further notice. All monetary values must be stated in local currency with two decimal places. Verbal approvals or email confirmations are strictly invalid for processing. The AssetCare system locks submitted forms against modification once the initial review timestamp is recorded. Requestors must retain a copy of the submitted form for their departmental archives for a minimum of thirty-six months. Any discrepancy between the portal record and the physical work order will default to the portal record as the authoritative source. To prevent pipeline saturation, each department operates under a strict quarterly request quota. The Mechanical Division is allocated 140 submissions per quarter, while the Electrical Division receives 110. The Pneumatics Unit is limited to 60. Quotas reset on the first calendar day of January, April, July, and October. Requests submitted after a department’s quota is exhausted are held in a pending state until the next quarter begins, unless they qualify for an emergency override.

2. Equipment Classification & Criticality Matrix
Maintenance priority and routing are determined by the asset’s classification tier. The classification rubric is applied automatically upon submission but may be manually adjusted by a certified reviewer. Assets are categorised based on two axes: operational impact score (OIS) and replacement threshold (RT). Tier 1 (Critical) applies when OIS ≥ 85 or RT > 45,000. Tier 2 (High) applies when OIS is between 60 and 84, or RT is between 20,000 and 44,999. Tier 3 (Standard) applies when OIS is between 30 and 59, or RT is between 5,000 and 19,999. Tier 4 (Low) applies when OIS < 30 and RT < 4,999. Borderline cases where OIS and RT fall into different tiers are classified according to the higher tier. If an asset’s OIS is exactly 60, it is classified as Tier 2. If the RT is exactly 20,000, it is classified as Tier 2. Assets undergoing major retrofit projects are temporarily suspended from this matrix and routed to the Capital Projects division regardless of scores.

3. Requestor Eligibility & Role Permissions
Only personnel with active credentials in the maintenance module may initiate requests. Junior Technicians may submit forms for Tier 3 and Tier 4 assets only. Senior Engineers may submit for Tier 2 and Tier 3 assets. Plant Managers hold unrestricted submission privileges across all tiers. Junior Technicians must attach a preliminary diagnostic report for any request exceeding 1,500 in estimated cost. Senior Engineers must provide a failure mode analysis for requests exceeding 8,000. Plant Manager submissions are exempt from diagnostic attachments but require a budget impact statement for any single request over 25,000. All requestors must confirm that the asset is not currently under a manufacturer warranty extension, as those require direct vendor routing. Permission levels are audited monthly, and any submission outside a role’s permitted tier range is automatically flagged for supervisor review.

4. Scheduling Windows & Operational Constraints
Maintenance activities must align with facility operational cycles. Standard maintenance windows are scheduled between 22:00 and 06:00 on weekdays, or any time on Saturdays. Sundays are reserved exclusively for Tier 1 critical repairs or emergency overrides. Blackout dates occur during the annual production surge, specifically from November 15 to December 10, during which only Tier 1 assets may be serviced. When scheduling conflicts arise between multiple pending requests, the system applies a weighted priority algorithm. The algorithm prioritises assets with the highest Tier classification first. If tiers are identical, priority shifts to the request with the longest queue time. If queue times are identical, the request with the lower estimated cost is prioritised to preserve capital liquidity. Manual rescheduling by floor supervisors requires a signed variance form and cannot override blackout dates or Sunday restrictions without Regional Director consent. All scheduled work must commence within the allocated window; work extending beyond the window requires a formal time-extension request submitted at least two hours before the window closes.

5. Approval Authority & Financial Limits
Financial authorisation follows a strict hierarchical threshold. Requests up to 5,000 may be approved by the requesting Senior Engineer. Requests between 5,001 and 15,000 require sign-off from the Departmental Maintenance Supervisor. Requests between 15,001 and 40,000 must be authorised by the Regional Operations Director. Any single request exceeding 40,000 requires dual approval from both the Regional Operations Director and the Chief Financial Officer. If a requestor’s department has exceeded its quarterly quota, the approval threshold for that department is temporarily reduced by 30% until the quota resets. For example, a department over quota may only secure Departmental Supervisor approval for requests up to 10,500. Splitting a single maintenance scope across multiple forms to bypass approval limits is strictly prohibited and will trigger an automatic audit. If an audit is triggered, all pending forms from that requestor are frozen for fourteen business days. Approval timestamps are recorded to the minute, and retroactive authorisations are invalid.

6. Reviewer Notes & Compliance Checklist
Every submitted form undergoes a mandatory compliance review before entering the scheduling queue. Reviewers must verify that the asset serial number matches the central registry, that the requestor holds valid clearance for the asset tier, and that all mandatory attachments are present. Reviewers are required to add a compliance note for any request where the estimated cost deviates by more than 15% from the last recorded maintenance event for the same asset. If a reviewer identifies a missing diagnostic report for a Junior Technician request over 1,500, the form is returned to the requestor for correction within forty-eight hours. Reviewers may also flag forms for budget reallocation if the requesting department’s quarterly spend has reached 85% of its annualised run rate. Flagged forms are routed to the Finance Liaison for secondary review. Reviewer notes become part of the permanent audit trail and cannot be deleted or altered after the form status changes to “Approved”. In cases where a reviewer notes a procedural violation, the form is automatically downgraded by one tier for scheduling purposes, regardless of its calculated classification. Reviewers do not verify inventory availability; this remains the requestor's sole responsibility.

7. Emergency Override & Exception Protocols
Emergency overrides bypass standard scheduling and approval queues for assets posing immediate safety hazards or causing complete production line stoppages. Overrides may only be initiated by a Plant Manager or a certified Safety Officer. The override process requires a verbal confirmation from the Regional Operations Director, followed by a written justification submitted within six hours of the override activation. Emergency overrides are subject to a strict financial cap of 35,000 per incident. Any costs exceeding this cap must be retroactively approved through the standard financial authority chain within five business days. Override activations automatically consume 10% of the requesting department’s remaining quarterly quota as an administrative penalty. If a department has already exhausted its quota, an override is still permitted but will trigger a mandatory post-incident review by the Compliance Committee. False or frivolous overrides, as determined by the Compliance Committee, result in the suspension of the initiator’s submission privileges for thirty days.

8. Processing Fees & Reimbursement Rules
All maintenance requests incur a standard administrative processing fee of 150, deducted from the requesting department’s operational budget. This fee is non-refundable once the form status reaches “In Progress”. If a maintenance task is cancelled by the facility management before work commences, the fee is waived and the department’s budget is restored. If the task is partially completed but does not resolve the reported failure, the fee is reduced to 75, and the remaining balance is returned to the department’s budget pool. However, if the partial completion is due to parts shortages caused by the requester’s failure to verify inventory availability prior to submission, the full 150 fee remains charged and no reimbursement is issued. Reimbursements for cancelled or partially completed tasks are processed during the monthly finance cycle and appear on departmental ledgers by the tenth business day of the following month. Any dispute regarding fee assessments must be filed with the Finance Liaison within ten business days of the ledger update.

instructions: Is the department entitled to a fee reimbursement of 75?
options: false
An exception clause overrides the general rule due to unverified inventory, voiding reimbursement.
true
Partial completion qualifies for standard reimbursement under the general fee rule.

Aethelgard Hospitality Group: Guest Reservation & Modification Policy Manual (v4.2)

1. Introduction & Scope
This policy governs all reservation activities across the Aethelgard Hospitality Group (AHG) portfolio, effective 1 November 2024. It applies to direct bookings, third-party agency placements, corporate contracts, and walk-in transactions. All staff members handling guest requests must adhere to the exact thresholds, dates, and role-based permissions outlined herein. Definitions: "Check-in date" refers to the first night of the confirmed stay. "Original payment method" denotes the card or account used at booking. "Manager" refers to any Front Office Supervisor or Duty Manager. "Regional Director" refers to the appointed executive for the property's geographic cluster.

2. Booking Channels & Rate Tiers
AHG properties operate four distinct rate tiers. Eligibility is strictly channel-dependent, as detailed in the table below. Third-party OTA bookings are excluded from all loyalty and corporate benefits. Peak Season dates are 15 December 2024 through 15 January 2025, and 1 July 2025 through 15 August 2025. During Peak Season, all reservations automatically convert to the Non-Refundable pricing structure, regardless of the tier initially selected by the guest.

Channel | Eligible Tiers
Direct Web | Standard, Flexible, Non-Refundable
Third-Party OTA | Standard, Non-Refundable
Corporate Portal | Flexible, Standard
Walk-in | Standard

3. Deposit Requirements & Pro-Rata Calculations
Deposit schedules are tier-specific. Standard bookings require a 20% deposit at confirmation, with the remaining 80% collected at check-in. Flexible bookings require a 50% deposit at confirmation, with the remaining 50% collected at check-out. Non-Refundable bookings require 100% payment at confirmation. Group reservations comprising five or more rooms bypass these deposit schedules but mandate a flat 30% upfront administrative fee. For partial cancellations or date modifications, refunds are strictly calculated on the actual nightly rate of the affected nights, not the average daily rate of the original stay. If a modified stay spans a rate change or seasonal boundary, the higher applicable rate applies to every night of the new itinerary.

4. Cancellation & Modification Windows
Standard and Flexible bookings permit free cancellation or date modification up to 48 hours prior to the scheduled check-in date. Non-Refundable bookings allow zero hours for cancellation or modification. Peak Season bookings enforce a strict 14-day window for all tiers. Each modification request submitted within the permitted window incurs a $75 administrative fee. If modified dates fall into a different rate tier or seasonal period, the new rate applies to the entire stay. The price difference is calculated as (New Total Rate − Original Total Rate). Adjustments exceeding $200 require explicit Manager approval before processing. Refunds for cancelled nights are processed to the original payment method within five business days.

5. Loyalty Program & Corporate Overrides
AHG Loyalty status modifies base windows and fees. Gold members receive a 24-hour extension to the base cancellation/modification window. Platinum members receive a full waiver of the $75 modification fee. Corporate bookings carrying a valid corporate identification number ending precisely in "CORP" receive a 72-hour window extension, overriding base tier restrictions. When both Loyalty and Corporate benefits apply, the Corporate window takes precedence. Loyalty benefits are strictly void for any reservation originated through Third-Party OTA channels. Corporate ID validation occurs at the time of the modification request; expired or malformed IDs revert the booking to base rules.

6. Force Majeure & Unforeseen Circumstances
AHG recognizes force majeure events including government-issued travel advisories, declared natural disasters, and official property closures. Guests affected by these events qualify for a full refund to the original payment method, processed within ten business days. Unforeseen personal illness or injury qualifies for a full refund only if accompanied by a hospital discharge summary dated within 48 hours of the original check-in date. Guests who have purchased third-party travel insurance must pursue claims directly with their provider; AHG will not process direct refunds if active insurance is detected on the booking profile, though we will supply required documentation upon request.

7. Precedence Rules & Request Routing Rubric
Policy sections follow a strict hierarchy in case of conflict: Section 6 > Section 5 > Section 4 > Section 3. Any financial adjustment or refund exceeding $500 requires Regional Director sign-off. All guest requests are classified into one of four routing categories based on the following rubric:
- Expedited: Cancellation/modification within window, AND (Platinum status OR valid Corporate ID). Processed immediately by staff.
- Standard: Within window, base tier, no overrides. Processed within 24 hours.
- Manager Review: Price difference adjustment strictly greater than $200, OR conflicting tier/loyalty status. Requires Manager sign-off.
- Denied: Outside window, Non-Refundable tier, or Peak Season booking without force majeure documentation. No action taken.
Boundary values (e.g., exactly 48 hours, exactly $200) fall into the more restrictive category unless explicitly waived by Section 5.

8. Administrative Notes
This manual supersedes all prior versions. Policy updates are issued quarterly. Staff must verify all dates, amounts, and IDs against the central reservation system before applying overrides. Questions regarding ambiguous cases must be escalated to the Revenue Management Office. Contact: policy.support@aethelgardhg.com | Ext. 4402.

Master Loan Servicing Agreement - Meridian Capital & Apex Services

1. SCOPE & DEFINITIONS
This Master Loan Servicing Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of January 15, 2024, between Meridian Capital Partners LLC ("Lender") and Apex Loan Services Ltd. ("Servicer"). The Agreement governs the administration, collection, and modification of the consumer auto and unsecured personal loan portfolio initially valued at $42,500,000 ("Portfolio"). All references to "Business Day" exclude weekends and federal banking holidays. "Outstanding Principal" refers to the unpaid balance before any accrued interest or fees. The Servicer shall act as an independent contractor, not an agent, unless explicitly required by regulatory statute. All operational standards must comply with the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and applicable state usury limits.

2. SERVICING FEES & REMUNERATION
The Lender shall pay the Servicer a monthly servicing fee calculated at 0.35% of the average daily Outstanding Principal. Fees are invoiced on the 5th of each month and payable by the 20th of the following month. A minimum monthly fee of $1,200 applies regardless of portfolio size. If the Portfolio balance falls below $10,000,000 for any consecutive 90-day period, the fee rate automatically adjusts to 0.50%, though the $1,200 minimum remains in effect. The Servicer must remit all collected principal, interest, and borrower fees to the Lender's designated trust account within three Business Days of receipt. Late remittance incurs a penalty of 1.5% per annum on the delayed amount, calculated daily.

3. LOAN MODIFICATIONS & PREPAYMENTS
Borrowers may request loan modifications, including interest rate adjustments, term extensions, or payment deferrals. Modifications are classified by loan balance into three tiers: Tier 1 ($50,000 and above), Tier 2 ($10,000 to $49,999), and Tier 3 (below $10,000). Each tier mandates a specific internal approval role before execution. Prepayments of the full outstanding balance are permitted at any time. If a prepayment occurs within the first eighteen months of the loan origination date, a prepayment penalty of two percent (2%) of the prepaid amount applies. The penalty is waived only if the borrower submits written notice to the Servicer at least fifteen Business Days before the scheduled payment date that triggers the prepayment. Partial prepayments do not trigger the penalty but must be applied to principal in order of maturity.

4. DEFAULT MANAGEMENT & COLLECTION
A loan enters default status if a scheduled payment is missed by more than thirty calendar days, the borrower files for bankruptcy, or fraud is substantiated. Upon default, the Servicer must assess a late fee equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue payment or $25, whichever is greater, assessed once per occurrence. Collection activities must commence within ten Business Days for defaults occurring in the fourth calendar quarter, and within fifteen Business Days for defaults in the first three quarters. The Servicer may engage third-party collection agencies for accounts exceeding 90 days past due, provided the agency holds valid state licenses. All communication with borrowers must document the date, time, and content of the interaction in the centralized case management system.

5. REPORTING, RECONCILIATION & APPROVAL AUTHORITY
The Servicer shall deliver monthly performance reports by the 10th calendar day of the following month. Reports must include delinquency aging, modification success rates, and remittance summaries. Reconciliation discrepancies exceeding $500 require joint sign-off by the Lender's Finance Director and the Servicer's Operations Lead. Approval authority for modifications and fee waivers is strictly capped by role: Operations Lead ($5,000), Regional Manager ($25,000), Senior Vice President ($150,000), and Portfolio Director ($500,000). Requests exceeding the designated role's limit must escalate to the next senior tier. The Servicer must maintain audit logs of all approval actions for a minimum of seven years.

6. TERM, TERMINATION & TRANSITION
The initial term of this Agreement is three years, commencing on January 15, 2024, and automatically renewing for successive one-year periods unless terminated. Termination for convenience requires written notice delivered at least forty-five calendar days prior to the intended effective date. The effective date must coincide with the last day of a calendar month. Termination for cause may be invoked immediately upon written notice if the Servicer breaches financial covenants, but non-financial breaches allow a fifteen-day cure period. Upon termination, the Servicer must transfer all borrower records, case files, and pending modification requests within ten Business Days. Transition fees shall be billed at the standard monthly rate, prorated daily.

7. PRECEDENCE & DISPUTE RESOLUTION
In the event of any inconsistency or conflict between provisions contained within this Agreement, the following strict order of precedence shall apply: (i) any executed Amendment signed by authorized representatives, (ii) attached Schedules, (iii) the main body of this Agreement. Where two provisions within the same hierarchical level conflict, the provision imposing the stricter compliance requirement shall prevail. Disputes arising from interpretation shall first be escalated to the joint steering committee. If unresolved within thirty days, disputes shall be submitted to binding arbitration under AAA commercial rules in Chicago, Illinois.

8. GENERAL PROVISIONS
This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations. Notices shall be deemed delivered three Business Days after dispatch via certified mail or on the date of confirmed electronic receipt. Neither party may assign this Agreement without prior written consent, except in connection with a merger or acquisition. If any provision is held invalid, the remainder shall continue in full force. The Servicer shall maintain cyber insurance coverage of no less than $5,000,000 per occurrence.
